claims.text: What the image looks like Dilated LV with EF ≤40%, global hypokinesis → HFrEF / dilated cardiomyopathy
claims.quote: Dilated LV with EF ≤40%, global hypokinesis HFrEF / dilated cardiomyopathy

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Systolic function (LVEF): HFrEF ≤40% / HFmrEF 41-49% / HFpEF ≥50%
claims.quote: Systolic function (LVEF): HFrEF ≤40% / HFmrEF 41-49% / HFpEF ≥50%.

claims.text: Chamber sizes: LV (LVEDD, LVESD), RV (> 1:1 with LV = dilated), LA, RA
claims.quote: Chamber sizes - LV (LVEDD, LVESD), RV (>1:1 with LV = dilated), LA, RA.

claims.text: Regional wall motion: 17-segment model; akinesis/hypokinesis suggests prior MI in a coronary distribution
claims.quote: Regional wall motion - 17-segment model; akinesis/hypokinesis suggests prior MI in coronary distribution.

claims.text: TTE characteristically shows LV dilation with global hypokinesis and atrial enlargement and excludes primary valve disease; functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation may result from annular dilation; regional wall motion abnormalities may occur
claims.quote: Transthoracic echocardiography characteristically demonstrates left ventricular dilation with global hypokinesis and atrial enlargement and excludes primary valvular disorders. Functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation may result from annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement (4). Although the typical pattern is one of diffuse hypokinesis, regional wall motion abnormalities may occur, reflecting the heterogeneous or patchy nature of myocardial involvement in DCM.

claims.text: Measuring LVEF distinguishes predominant HFpEF (EF ≥ 50%) from HFrEF (EF ≤ 40%); heart failure can occur with a normal LVEF
claims.quote: Measuring LVEF can distinguish between predominant HFpEF (EF ≥ 50%) and HFrEF (EF ≤ 40%). It is important to re-emphasize that heart failure can occur with a normal LVEF.

claims.text: CXR may show an enlarged cardiac silhouette, splaying of the carina, interstitial edema and pleural effusions
claims.quote: Chest radiograph may reveal an enlarged cardiac silhouette, splaying of the carina, interstitial edema, and pleural effusions.

claims.text: Natriuretic peptides are typically elevated and give diagnostic and prognostic information
claims.quote: Laboratory testing includes natriuretic peptides, which are typically elevated and provide both diagnostic and prognostic information (2, 3).

claims.text: An ischemia evaluation should be done to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease as the cause of LV systolic dysfunction
claims.quote: Given the high prevalence of coronary artery disease, an ischemia evaluation should be performed to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease as the cause of LV systolic dysfunction.

claims.text: Causes DCM: LV or biventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction without congenital heart disease, abnormal loading (eg, primary valve disease) or coronary artery disease sufficient to explain it
claims.quote: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a primary myocardial disorder, defined as the presence of left ventricular or biventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction in the absence of congenital heart disease, abnormal loading conditions (eg, primary valve disease), or coronary artery disease sufficient to account for the observed ventricular remodelling.

claims.text: Familial in approximately 30 to 40% (TTN and LMNA most commonly implicated); acquired: infections (eg, coxsackievirus B, Trypanosoma cruzi in endemic regions), toxins (eg, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy), tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy, and systemic disorders (eg, thyrotoxicosis, thiamine deficiency)
claims.quote: Familial disease is present in approximately 30 to 40% of cases, with monogenic variants identified in a substantial proportion (25 to 40%) of these patients (1). TTN and LMNA are the most commonly implicated genes in DCM. Acquired etiologies include infections (eg, coxsackievirus B, Trypanosoma cruzi in endemic regions), toxins (eg, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapeutic agents), tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy, and systemic disorders, including autoimmune, endocrine (eg, thyrotoxicosis), nutritional (eg, thiamine deficiency), and neuromuscular diseases (see table ).

claims.text: Dilation and reduced contractility predispose to intracardiac thrombus (stasis); atrial fibrillation frequently develops with LA enlargement; ventricular arrhythmias may occur
claims.quote: Phenotypically, dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction, frequently accompanied by compensatory eccentric hypertrophy, atrial dilation, and functional mitral regurgitation and/or tricuspid regurgitation. Both ventricles are frequently involved (1). Ventricular dilation and reduced contractility predispose to intracardiac thrombus formation due to stasis of blood. Atrial fibrillation frequently develops in the setting of left atrial enlargement (2), and ventricular arrhythmias may occur, particularly in the context of acute myocarditis or in the presence of myocardial fibrosis (3, 4, 5, 6).

claims.text: Symptoms LV systolic dysfunction most commonly → exertional dyspnea, orthopnea and fatigue; RV involvement → peripheral edema, hepatomegaly, abdominal distension and elevated JVP
claims.quote: Clinical manifestations reflect the predominant ventricular involvement. Left ventricular systolic dysfunction most commonly leads to exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and fatigue, which is attributable to elevated left-sided filling pressures and/or reduced cardiac output. Right ventricular involvement results in systemic venous congestion, manifesting as peripheral edema, hepatomegaly, abdominal distension, and elevated jugular venous pressure.

claims.text: Exam may include an S3 or S4 gallop, a mitral or tricuspid regurgitation murmur, a displaced PMI, and pulsus alternans in severe cases
claims.quote: Other cardiac findings on examination may include an S3 or S4 gallop, a mitral or tricuspid regurgitation murmur, a displaced point of maximal impulse, and, in severe cases, pulsus alternans.

claims.text: Patients may also present with atrial and ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death from malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias
claims.quote: Patients may also present with atrial and ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death due to malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: GDMT: ARNI/ACEI, β-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i; ICD if EF ≤35%
claims.quote: GDMT: ARNI/ACEI, β-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i; ICD if EF ≤35%

claims.text: GDMT for HFrEF reduces morbidity and mortality: beta blockers, ARNi (or ACE inhibitor or ARB if ARNi not feasible), MRA and SGLT2i, with diuretics for volume
claims.quote: Patients with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) should be treated with guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF because these agents reduce morbidity and mortality (2). The cornerstones of treatment include beta blockers, angiotensin receptor/neprilysin inhibitor (ARNi) (or angiotensin-converting enzyme [ACE] inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) if ARNi not feasible), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA), and sodium glucose cotransporter-2 protein inhibitors (SGLT2i), with diuretics for volume management (3, 4).

claims.text: Identify and treat reversible causes (eg, tachyarrhythmias, infections, metabolic or nutritional disorders)
claims.quote: Reversible causes (eg, tachyarrhythmias, infections, metabolic or nutritional disorders) should be identified and treated (1).

claims.text: ICD for primary prevention with symptoms and persistent LVEF ≤ 35% despite chronic GDMT; CRT with symptoms, LVEF ≤ 35% and QRS prolongation, particularly with LBBB
claims.quote: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy is recommended for primary prevention in patients with symptoms and persistent LVEF ≤ 35% despite chronic guideline-directed medical therapy, and cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is indicated in patients with symptoms with LVEF ≤ 35% and QRS prolongation, particularly in the presence of a left bundle branch block (3, 4).

claims.text: Anticoagulation may be considered with documented intracardiac thrombus, and atrial fibrillation
claims.quote: Anticoagulation may be considered in patients with documented intracardiac thrombus, and atrial fibrillation (3, 5, 6).
